title: Diamonds and gold
summary: Within twenty years, diamonds at Kimberley and gold on the Witwatersrand turned a farming region into an industrial economy. Mining built Johannesburg, the migrant labour system and the fortunes behind the next war.
caveat: Well documented in company records, colonial reports and newspapers. The experiences of Black miners are recorded less fully than those of owners and officials.

stops.title: The Eureka diamond
stops.narration: A boy named Erasmus Jacobs picked up a shiny pebble on his family's farm near the Orange River. It turned out to be a 21-carat diamond.
sources: Martin Meredith, Diamonds, Gold and War (2007)

stops.title: The Big Hole
stops.narration: Diamonds were found on a small hill, and thousands of diggers turned it into a pit. By 1888 Cecil Rhodes had merged the claims into De Beers, and Black workers were housed in closed compounds.
sources: Martin Meredith, Diamonds, Gold and War (2007)
Rob Turrell, Capital and Labour on the Kimberley Diamond Fields, 1871-1890 (1987)

stops.title: Pilgrim's Rest
stops.narration: Alluvial gold in this valley drew diggers to the eastern escarpment. The village is preserved much as the mining camp left it.
sources: Martin Meredith, Diamonds, Gold and War (2007)

stops.title: Barberton
stops.narration: A gold boom here created the region's first stock exchange. It faded fast, but it trained the prospectors who went to the Witwatersrand.
sources: Martin Meredith, Diamonds, Gold and War (2007)

stops.title: The Main Reef
stops.narration: Prospectors found the outcrop of the Main Reef on the farm Langlaagte. Johannesburg was laid out months later and grew into South Africa's largest city.
stops.confidence_note: The marker shows central Johannesburg; Langlaagte lies a few kilometres west.
sources: Martin Meredith, Diamonds, Gold and War (2007)
Charles van Onselen, New Babylon, New Nineveh (1982)

stops.title: The Jameson Raid ends
stops.narration: A force backed by Rhodes tried to spark an uprising of foreign miners against the Transvaal government and surrendered here. Rhodes resigned, and trust between Briton and Boer collapsed.
sources: Martin Meredith, Diamonds, Gold and War (2007)
